# `Q-5-9` — Pre-render script changed a forbidden project setting

> A `project.pre-render` script changed `project.type` or
> `project.output-dir` in `_quarto.yml`, which must stay fixed.

## What this means

Pre-render scripts are allowed to modify the project. Generating input
files, rewriting configuration, adding entries to a listing — all of
that is supported and is much of why the hook exists.

Two settings are the exception: `project.type` and
`project.output-dir`. Quarto reads both *before* running the scripts,
because it has to — the scripts themselves receive
`QUARTO_PROJECT_OUTPUT_DIR` in their environment, computed from those
values. A script that changes them afterwards has already been handed
the old answer, and the render that follows would use a mix of the two.

Quarto detects the change by re-reading `_quarto.yml` after the scripts
finish, and reports it rather than proceeding with an inconsistent
configuration.

## Why this happens

- **A script that rewrites `_quarto.yml` wholesale**, regenerating the
  whole file from a template and changing these keys as a side effect
  of reordering or reformatting.
- **Switching output directories per environment** — a script that sets
  `output-dir: _site-staging` when a staging variable is set.
- **Switching project type conditionally**, for instance between
  `default` and `website`.

## How to fix

Move these two settings out of the script and into `_quarto.yml`
directly:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: _site
  pre-render: tools/prepare.py
```

If the value genuinely needs to vary, use a project profile rather than
a script. Profiles are resolved before scripts run, so the setting is
fixed by the time the environment variables are computed:

```yaml
# _quarto-staging.yml
project:
  output-dir: _site-staging
```

```bash
quarto render --profile staging
```

If the script is rewriting `_quarto.yml` from a template, have the
template carry the current values rather than defaults — reading them
back before writing is the reliable form.
